summary: On 28 February 2012 (29 February UTC) Windows Azure's guest agents tried to create certificates valid for one year by adding one to the year. On leap day that produced 29 February 2013, which does not exist, and compute service management failed worldwide.

overview.background: Each Windows Azure guest agent (GA) creates a transfer certificate with a one-year validity so it can talk securely to its host. The fabric controller manages servers and, on repeated failures, marks hardware as bad.
systems: Compute, Access Control Service, Service Bus, Caching
SQL Azure Portal and Data Sync
overview.impact: A partial outage of Windows Azure Compute and dependent services. Storage and SQL Azure were not affected. Customers could not deploy, update, stop or scale applications, and some VMs went offline.
overview.severity: Global, with a secondary outage in seven clusters. Microsoft gave a 33 percent service credit to affected customers.
overview.gaps: The post gives no VM counts.

archNote: Components and relationships come from the cited source where it describes them. Layout and labels are ours.

diagrams.title: A date calculation fails and the fabric blames hardware
diagrams.caption: The GA added one to the year and got an invalid date. Certificate creation failed, the GA terminated, and repeated failures made the fabric controller treat servers as faulty.

nodes.label: Fabric Controller counts failures, flags servers

diagrams.title: Better testing and finer controls (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: Microsoft listed time-bug testing, fault isolation, finer-grained disabling of service parts and clearer dashboards. This picture shows the idea.

nodes.label: Tests for dates such as leap days
Software faults separated from hardware faults
Disable parts of the service, not all of it
Dashboard with a summary of the situation

afterChanges: Time bugs are caught before release.
A software bug is not treated as a hardware failure.
Operators can pause only what is unsafe.

timelineNote: Times are as published by the source. Entries without a clock time are given in order only.

timeline.e: The bug triggers as new VMs try to create certificates.
The Human Investigate threshold is reached in clusters being updated.
Service management is disabled in all clusters worldwide, the first time this step was taken.
The fix completes rollout to one production cluster, then is pushed to all clusters.
An incompatible combination of components is pushed to seven clusters, causing a secondary outage.
Service management is restored to most clusters.
The seven clusters are largely operational.
The dashboard reports all services healthy.

rootCause.trigger: On leap day any GA creating a transfer certificate set a valid-to date of 29 February 2013.
rootCause.underlying: The code added one to the current year without handling leap day, so certificate creation failed and the GA terminated.
contributing: The fabric controller treated repeated failures as hardware faults
A fix pushed in a hurry was incompatible with some components
The dashboard and communication were weak
Dependent services such as ACS and Service Bus needed prioritised recovery
propagation: Management is disabled to stop the spread.

evidence.label: The bug
evidence.body: any GA that tried to create a transfer certificate on leap day set a valid-to date of February 29, 2013

evidence.label: The lesson
evidence.body: The three truths of cloud computing are: hardware fails, software has bugs and people make mistakes.

evidence.label: A simulated date bug
evidence.body:
from datetime import date
today = date(2012, 2, 29)
valid_to = today.replace(year=today.year + 1)  # ValueError: day is out of range
evidence.note: Reproduces the class of bug in Python. Not Azure code.

diagnose.step: Check what is common to the failing machines.
diagnose.why: All failures started at the same moment, so a date or clock was the clue.

diagnose.step: Read the agent's error for the certificate step.
diagnose.why: The failure was in creating the certificate.

diagnose.step: Check whether the fabric is blaming hardware.
diagnose.why: Repeated failures were wrongly flagged as hardware faults.

correct.step: Stop changes that spread the failure.
Fix the date calculation and test it first.
correct.why: The fix was tested on a test cluster.

correct.step: Roll out the fix cluster by cluster.

verify.step: Check the fabric reports healthy servers.
verify.why: Confirm the false hardware flags clear.
ACS and Service Bus recovered separately.

prevent.step: Test dates around leap days and year ends.
Separate software faults from hardware faults.

fix.safety: Disabling service management stops customers changing their apps, but it protects running ones. Announce it clearly.

troubleshoot.scenario: Every new VM fails to start on the same minute and servers are being marked bad. Today is 29 February.
clues: All clusters show the same errors
troubleshoot.question: How do you find and contain the cause?
hints: How do you test the fix?
troubleshoot.answer: Notice the shared timing, find the certificate date error, stop service management, fix and test the date logic, roll out in stages and check fabric hardware flags.

rootcause.q: What date did the GA compute?

remediation.answer: Include 29 February, 28 February in a leap year, year end and time zone boundaries.
Separate software errors from hardware by symptom and spread.
Test, one cluster, then more, with compatibility checks.

design.prompt: Design certificate creation that cannot fail on a date.
design.answer: Use a date library that adds a year safely, test edge dates, handle failure by retry and alert rather than terminate, and avoid failing hard.

checks.why: Microsoft says storage and SQL Azure were not affected.

checks.q: What was the first time Microsoft took which step?
checks.why: Microsoft says it was the first time.

options: An incompatible combination of components pushed to seven clusters

preventive: Separate software faults from hardware faults
Finer controls to disable parts of a service
practices: Plan for hardware fails, software has bugs, people make mistakes
